s.note: Air hisses through a narrow passage behind the teeth.

ʒ.note: Like /ʃ/ with the vocal folds vibrating.

d.note: The tongue briefly closes the airflow behind the upper teeth.

f.note: Air passes between the lower lip and upper teeth.
f.definition: A body part a fish uses for swimming.

t.note: The tongue releases a brief closure behind the upper teeth.

z.note: A hiss like /s/ with vibration in the throat.
z.definition: A place where animals are kept for visitors.

v.note: Like /f/ with the vocal folds vibrating.

e.note: A close-mid front vowel with unrounded lips.

i.note: A close front vowel with unrounded lips.

ɛ.note: The mouth is more open than for /e/.

a.note: An open vowel with unrounded lips.

ɔ.note: An open-mid back vowel with rounded lips.

u.note: The tongue is high and back and the lips are rounded.

o.note: A close-mid back vowel with rounded lips.

ɑ.note: An open back vowel with unrounded lips in this American pronunciation.

h.note: Air flows freely through the open glottis.

k.note: The back of the tongue briefly touches the soft palate.
k.definition: A small tool for opening a lock.

p.note: Air is released after both lips close.
p.definition: A tool for writing with ink.

b.note: Both lips close to make this voiced stop.
b.definition: A container for storage or waste.
